competitor_alerts: NEW COMPETITOR: Shi-Ya Modern Asian Cuisine, a 100% kosher sushi restaurant, opened June 28, 2026 at 7114 Campbell Road inside Meat Point. Covered by the Dallas Observer AND CravedDFW in July 2026 — that is two authoritative local-press backlinks earned in one quarter, which is how Meat Point keeps outranking us for 'kosher restaurant Dallas'.

Simcha Kosher Catering is the single strongest organic competitor for 'kosher catering Dallas': it occupies three separate page-1 slots (own site, Facebook page, Yelp listing with 11 reviews). We hold one slot at position 10.
A Taste of the World has a dedicated /dallas-kosher-catering landing page and ranks twice on page 1 for 'kosher catering Dallas' — an exact-match URL strategy we are not using.

Aggregator platforms (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Postmates, Grubhub, Yelp) own the entire first page for both delivery keywords. Natalie's Kitchen ranks for 'kosher delivery Dallas' purely through its Grubhub listing despite being a smaller operation.

Directory sites — Dallas Kosher, DOJLife, TotallyJewishTravel, Mekomos, Restaurant Guru, Wanderlog, ezCater, Menustic — appear on nearly every keyword. We already have listings on several (ezCater, TotallyJewishTravel, Mekomos, Dallas Kosher) but they rank instead of our own site.
Kosher Palate (7989 Belt Line Rd) and Deli News Frisco appear in catering results but have no page-1 organic presence of their own, so they are beatable targets rather than threats.

New kosher dairy option: J's Kosher Dairy Kitchen opened in 2026, and Pure Green kosher juice bar opened in Plano (April 2026) — the Dallas kosher market is expanding, increasing competition for the generic 'kosher food Dallas' term.

recommendations.action: Fix the openingHours error in the Restaurant JSON-LD on app/page.tsx. It currently declares "Mo-Th 10:00-20:00" and "Su 10:00-18:00", but the site footer and the ezCater/Yelp listings all say Mon-Fri 9:00am-2:00pm CST, closed Saturday and Sunday. Change it to ["Mo-Fr 09:00-14:00"].
recommendations.reason: This is the most damaging technical issue found this run. The structured data tells Google we are open Sunday evenings and until 8pm on weekdays when we are actually closed. Google surfaces these hours in the local pack and Knowledge Panel, so customers are being told to order when nobody is there — and conflicting hours signals across the site, schema, and third-party listings suppress local pack ranking, which is exactly where we are absent for all five 'Dallas' keywords.

recommendations.action: Add aggregateRating and Review schema to the homepage JSON-LD, sourced from the reviews already collected on /reviews. The current jsonLd object has no aggregateRating property at all.
recommendations.reason: We have genuinely strong review content — verified 10/10 ratings on ezCater and praise on Yelp, TotallyJewishTravel and Wanderlog for delivery packaging and salad freshness — and none of it is machine-readable. Star ratings in search results lift click-through substantially, and it is the cheapest available differentiator against Simcha Kosher Catering, whose Yelp listing shows only 11 reviews. We have a /reviews page and a /api/submit-review endpoint already built, so the data pipeline exists.

recommendations.reason: 'Kosher catering Dallas' is our best-performing keyword at position 10 and our highest-margin service, so it is the cheapest win available — but position 10 is the last slot on page 1 and gets a fraction of the clicks of position 3. recommendations.action: Correct the sameAs array in the homepage JSON-LD: it points to facebook.com/thehungryrooster, but the actual page linked in the site footer is facebook.com/thehungryroostertx. recommendations.action: Add a FoodEstablishment 'areaServed' property to the JSON-LD naming Dallas, Richardson, Plano, and Far North Dallas, and consider adding hasOfferCatalog entries for the Shabbat Box tiers ($65 / $115 / $225).
recommendations.reason: Competitors explicitly name their service areas — A Taste of the World lists Dallas, Plano, Richardson, and Fort Worth — and the Dallas kosher community is concentrated in Richardson and North Dallas around Coit, Preston, and Belt Line, not downtown where our Regal Row kitchen sits. Naming those suburbs helps us surface for neighborhood-level searches. The meta-keywords tag on every page can also be dropped; Google has ignored it since 2009 and it publishes our keyword targets to competitors.

quick_wins: Change openingHours in app/page.tsx JSON-LD from ["Mo-Th 10:00-20:00", "Su 10:00-18:00"] to ["Mo-Fr 09:00-14:00"] — one line, fixes actively wrong hours in Google's local pack.

Add lastModified dates and republish the two existing 2025 blog posts with refreshed 2026 content, and add both to the sitemap with current dates — the sitemap still hardcodes July 2025.
Create a /kosher-catering-dallas exact-match URL that redirects to or canonicalizes with /catering, mirroring the approach A Taste of the World uses to rank twice on page 1.
summary: We hold only two page-1 positions across seven target keywords — position 10 for 'kosher catering Dallas' and position 9 for 'Jewish catering Dallas' — and are absent entirely for 'kosher food Dallas', 'kosher restaurant Dallas', 'Shabbat meals Dallas', 'kosher delivery Dallas', and 'kosher meal delivery Texas'. The audit found a genuinely damaging bug: the homepage Restaurant schema declares Monday-Thursday 10am-8pm and Sunday hours, while the kitchen is actually open Monday-Friday 9am-2pm and closed weekends, so Google is publishing wrong hours to customers. Meanwhile a new kosher sushi restaurant, Shi-Ya, opened inside Meat Point in June and earned two local-press backlinks in a quarter, and the blog has not been updated since July 2025 — fixing the schema, adding review markup, and restarting content are this week's priorities.
